eligibility: COG/NCTN sites use the Appendix 7 criteria, which differ from the main ANZUP protocol.
Age ≥ 11 and ≤ 50 years at randomization.
Histologically or cytologically confirmed GCT (non-seminoma or seminoma), or AFP ≥ 1000 ng/mL and/or HCG ≥ 5000 IU/L without histology when metastatic pattern, high burden, and urgency fit GCT.
Primary in testis, ovary, retroperitoneum, or mediastinum; metastatic disease or non-testicular primary.

Intermediate or poor risk by modified IGCCC: non-seminoma intermediate (testis/retroperitoneal primary, no non-pulmonary visceral mets, AFP 1000-10,000 ng/mL, HCG 5000-50,000 IU/L, or LDH 3-10 x ULN); non-seminoma poor (mediastinal primary, non-pulmonary visceral mets, AFP > 10,000, HCG > 50,000, or LDH > 10 x ULN); seminoma with non-pulmonary visceral mets and normal AFP; or ovarian MGCT FIGO/COG stage IV. Post-orchiectomy markers used.
ANC ≥ 1.0 x 10^9/L and platelets ≥ 100 x 10^9/L.
Bilirubin ≤ 1.5 x ULN (≤ 2.0 x ULN with Gilbert's); AST/ALT ≤ 2.5 x ULN (≤ 5 x ULN with liver metastases).
Age ≥ 18: CrCl ≥ 60 mL/min (Cockcroft-Gault, or measured GFR if borderline). Age < 18: CrCl or GFR > 60 mL/min/1.73 m2 or creatinine at or below the age/sex maximum.
ECOG 0-3 equivalent (Karnofsky if > 16 years, Lansky if ≤ 16). Treatment able to start within 14 days of OPEN enrollment.
No prior chemotherapy or radiotherapy, except pure seminoma relapsing after adjuvant radiotherapy or 1-2 doses of single-agent carboplatin.
No other primary malignancy except treated non-melanoma skin cancer, GCT, or a cancer treated at least 5 years ago without recurrence.
No cardiac disease preventing cisplatin hydration, no respiratory disease contraindicating bleomycin, no grade ≥ 2 neuropathy, and no clinically significant hearing loss or tinnitus.
No severe concurrent illness or infection. No known allergy to study drugs.
Not pregnant; negative pregnancy test within 7 days before registration for women of childbearing potential.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Prospective single-arm phase II study (ePRO-PICCRT) of locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma. Primary endpoint is pathologic complete response. Assignment after the first cycle depends on patient-reported dysphagia relief, not randomization.

schema.label: Treatment
schema.text: Cycle 1 for all patients: albumin-bound paclitaxel 260 mg/m2 on day 1, carboplatin AUC 5 or cisplatin 60 mg/m2 on day 1, and tislelizumab 200 mg on day 1. Early remission is more than 70% relief on the EORTC OES-18 dysphagia score. That group continues the same regimen for two further cycles. The latent-remission group receives one further cycle, then short-course radiotherapy 30 Gy in 10 daily fractions of 3 Gy (days 1 to 5 and 16 to 20) with tislelizumab 200 mg on day 2, albumin-bound paclitaxel 60 mg/m2 on days 1, 8, and 15, and carboplatin AUC 2 on days 1, 8, and 15 or cisplatin 60 mg/m2 on day 1. Radical esophagectomy with lymphadenectomy is planned 4 to 6 weeks later. Voluntary immunotherapy every 3 weeks for up to 1 year may follow surgery.

brief.schema_source: Open-access protocol, Huang et al., Journal of Thoracic Disease 2024 (PMID 39144362). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Pathologically confirmed, treatment-naive, potentially resectable esophageal squamous cell carcinoma: cT1 to 4a N1 to 2 M0 or cT3 to 4a N0 M0. Age 18 to 75. Expected survival over 6 months. ECOG 0 to 2. Adequate organ function, without numeric cutoffs in the criteria list.

Excluded: prior thoracic surgery or radiation, cervical or multi-origin esophageal cancer, fistula, peripheral neuropathy, another cancer, autoimmune or immunodeficiency disease, diabetes longer than 10 years or poor control, interstitial lung disease, active hepatitis B or C, and pregnancy or lactation.

arms.label: Cohort 1: Gross-total resection, non-metastatic, early radiotherapy
arms.text: Participants will undergo gross total resection of the tumor prior to enrollment into this cohort. Standard dose induction chemotherapy and 6-weeks of early focal radiotherapy, followed by and a second standard dose induction chemotherapy for a total of 12 weeks of chemotherapy; 18 weeks of treatments in all. Participants will be followed for up to 2 years.

arms.label: Cohort 2: Gross-total resection, non-metastatic, high-dose chemotherapy
arms.text: Participants will undergo gross total resection of the tumor prior to enrollment into this cohort. Participants will receive 6 weeks of induction chemotherapy and 3 cycles (approximately 4 weeks each) of high-dose chemotherapy with stem cell rescue and will have the option to receive radiotherapy at the completion of therapy, for a total of 18-24 weeks. Participants will be followed for up to 2 years.

registry_schema.label: Design
registry_schema.text: The role of postoperative radiotherapy in thymoma is controversial. Some retrospective studies were for the radiotherapy, but others were against. However, more inherent biases existed in these trials. Resection, Masaoka stage and pathology were widely accepted as the prognostic factors for thymoma. Furthermore, the frequency of local failure after radical resection was still high in Masaoka stage II-III B type thymoma. With the conformal technique appearing, conformal radiotherapy can escalate the dose without increasing the risk of normal tissue toxicities.
